quote: But what set humanity firmly on the path of Science was noticing that certain modes of thinking uncovered beliefs that let us manipulate the world.
content: Craft preceding formal science does not reverse the feedback argument: useful interventions can reveal which beliefs track the world before their practitioners possess a mature theory. The sentence says noticing that some ways of thinking support manipulation helped establish science, not that theoretical science invented every earlier technology. Its sweeping origin story needs historical support, but Fable's technology-before-theory observation is compatible with the proposed direction of learning.

quote: it has a special and admirable purity
content: Choosing which question to investigate and choosing which answer to accept are different operations. Aesthetic interest can select an astronomy problem over an equally tractable accounting problem without supplying any evidence for either answer. The essay itself says curiosity can neglect verification, so Fable has identified a limitation that the argument uses to motivate an additional check.

quote: (Thankfully not many have questioned what truth is.)
content: A disagreement about the ultimate analysis of truth need not prevent agreement that the bookcase either occupies this location or does not. Deflationists and correspondence theorists can both distinguish a forecast that succeeds from one that fails. The aside is dismissive, but Fable has not shown that resolving the metaphysics of facts is a prerequisite for improving ordinary empirical beliefs.
